description:
FILED s515a (Opus, 2026-10-11) from Fable's review probe ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s513/review/p515a/iso-dup2.pl.  PRE-EXISTING (base and tree alike), LOW.
`my $buf = ""; open(my $s, ">", \$buf); open(my $t, ">&", $s); print $t "mem"; print $s "+s"; close $t; close $s; print "buf=[$buf]\n";` -- perl `buf=[+s]` (a dup of an in-memory handle does not write into the scalar), PCL `buf=[mem+s]`.  The fd-less branch of %p-open-dup shares (now aliases) the in-memory stream for `>&` as well as `>&=`; its comment already calls the `>&` case an approximation.  Related: a `>&=` of an in-memory handle -- perl's writes through it vanish too ("one three"), PCL writes them.


=== s519a (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-18): measured, NOT fixed -- not a small change in that branch ===
Probe scratch/s519a/pr/dup1.pl (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL on fca3593b+s519a): `>&` buf perl [+s] PCL [mem+s]; `>&=` perl [two three] PCL [one two three]; `<&` of an in-memory READ handle: perl reads l1 from the dup AND l1 again from the source, PCL l1 then l2.  So perl's model is not "writes vanish": a dup of a PerlIO :scalar handle is a NEW scalar layer on the SAME scalar with its OWN position (output: both start at 0 and overwrite each other; input: the dup starts where the source is and they advance independently) -- for `>&=` too.  The fix is a second in-memory stream over the same scalar with an independent position, not a one-line change in %p-open-dup's fd-less branch (which shares the stream object).  Left filed.
subject: a dup (>&) of an in-memory handle writes into the scalar -- perl's does not (buf=[+s] vs PCL buf=[mem+s])
